title: Bootstrap executable Foundation substrate and focused probes

evidence: npm run check: exit 0; 0 errors and 0 warnings
npm run test: exit 0; 1 file and 4 tests passed
targeted composition and atomicity reruns: 1/1 and 2/2 passed
boundary-scope probe: two allowed roots, one composition root, no adapter direct writes, no forbidden product roots

evidence_required: REQ-000 project-native baseline: RED = execution records the pre-bootstrap absence of a runnable package/scripts; GREEN = the created skeleton passes npm run check, npm run build, and npm run test; artifact = .protocols/TASK-001-T3-FT-000-W0/progress.md and verification.md.

system-architecture.md#composition-and-request-data-flow: RED = the composition/request path cannot wire one server to the accepted public seams; GREEN = a focused isolated harness observes one composition root with Identity & Access and Center & Scheduling boundary calls and no cross-slice table write; artifact = .protocols/TASK-001-T3-FT-000-W0/verification.md.

core-domain.md#persistence-and-transaction-rules: RED = an isolated fixture cannot round-trip or a failed binding/transaction changes persisted state; GREEN = state-before and state-after are identical after the failed probe, with safe rerun and cleanup; artifact = .tasks/TASK-001-T3-FT-000-W0/ and .protocols/TASK-001-T3-FT-000-W0/verification.md.
purpose: Establish the minimum executable SvelteKit/shared-database substrate and focused Foundation probes required before any product feature task can run.
success_outcome: A project-native SvelteKit skeleton passes check/build/test, exposes one composition root and one configured shared-database path, and the focused harness can reach only the accepted Identity & Access and Center & Scheduling public seams while proving isolated roundtrip and no-partial failure behavior.
anti_goals: Do not implement product calendar, collaboration, learning-progress, or financial behavior.
Do not create empty future capability slices, layer-centric modules, an event bus, a second server, or a shared cross-slice repository.
Do not select a new architecture or widen the accepted storage/provider contracts.
Do not create product task records or close the final Foundation gate.

stop_conditions: A probe requires product behavior or a capability slice beyond Identity & Access and Center & Scheduling.
A concrete database/provider choice changes an accepted architecture, boundary, ownership, or security contract.
The walking skeleton requires a second server, event bus, cache, shared cross-slice repository, or another speculative platform layer.

constraints: Use one SvelteKit server and one shared database path with a single composition root.
Keep browser/HTTP adapters thin; public boundary calls retain server-side actor/scope checks and slice write ownership.
Use isolated/disposable fixture state with safe rerun and cleanup.
Keep database engine/migration library and exact provider SDK configuration at execution-level choice unless a material design branch appears.
invariants: The shared database is the persisted source of truth, but each mutable business state has one capability write owner.
Protected operations resolve actor and scope on the server; client-supplied role or scope is not trusted.
Failed binding or transaction probes leave no partial state.
No request or user state is stored in server module scope.
verification_targets: Run npm run check, npm run build, and npm run test after bootstrap; the focused test target covers only Foundation substrate probes.
Use a disposable isolated fixture to prove schema/adapter roundtrip and state-before/state-after equality after a failed binding/transaction; rerun the probe after cleanup.

Review .memory-bank/architecture/system-architecture.md#composition-and-request-data-flow and .memory-bank/contracts/boundary-map.md#modules against the created composition root and the two allowed slice roots; report any boundary or ownership drift as a stop condition.
Use test doubles for provider failure/reuse/duplicate paths; do not require real Telegram/Google credentials or implement product provider flows in Foundation.
